children: Norway's annual core inflation rate rose to 3.0% year-on-year in August, Statistics Norway (SSB) data showed on Thursday, supporting expectations interest rates could increase further this year.
The core inflation, which strips out changing energy prices and taxes, rose from 2.7% in July and was in line with the 3.0% expected by analysts in a Reuters poll.
Norges Bank had expected core inflation of 3.3%.
Norway's currency, the crown, traded largely unchanged against the euro at 10.70 following the 0600 GMT data release.
Norway's central bank in August kept its policy interest rate on hold at 4.25% and said the future path of monetary policy would "depend on economic developments".
It had previously said interest rates would likely be raised at "one of the forthcoming monetary policy meetings".
The central bank, which targets core inflation of 2.0%, is scheduled to make its next rate announcement on September 24.
